content: 1. Central nervous system (CNS) depressants, such as skeletal muscle relaxants, can lead to respiratory depression, hypotension, profound sedation, coma, or even death. Dose adjustments for either or both agents should be considered to minimize the risk of severe adverse effects. Close monitoring for signs of hypotension, respiratory depression, and profound sedation is essential. 2. The combination of fentanyl transmucosal and opium tincture increases sedation due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Alternative therapies should be considered to avoid serious risks. 3. Co-administration of opium tincture with fluphenazine, flurazepam, or haloperidol enhances sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Opium tincture increases sedation when combined with formoterol, although formoterol may decrease sedation. The interaction's effect is unclear; proceed with caution and monitor. 5. Ganaxolone, hydromorphone, hydroxyzine, iloperidone, and imipramine all increase sedation when used with opium tincture. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. The combination of opium tincture with isocarboxazid poses a serious risk due to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The risk includes hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. A 14-day separation is recommended. 7. Isoproterenol decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 8. Ketamine, ketotifen (ophthalmic), lasmiditan, lemborexant, and levetiracetam all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Adjust therapy as needed and monitor closely. 9. Levalbuterol decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 10. Levocetirizine, levorphanol, lidocaine, and linezolid increase sedation or toxicity when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely for CNS depression. 11. Lisdexamfetamine decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 12. Lofepramine, lofexidine, lorazepam, lormetazepam, and loxapine all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Lumateperone and lurasidone increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 14. Maprotiline, marijuana, meclizine, melatonin, and meperidine all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Metaproterenol decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 16. Methadone, methamphetamine, methocarbamol, methohexital, and methsuximide all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Methylene-dioxymethamphetamine decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 18. Metoclopramide (intranasal) increases the effects of opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely for excessive CNS toxicity. 19. Midazolam (including intranasal) increases sedation when combined with opium tincture. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Midodrine decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 21. Mirtazapine, modafinil, molindone, morphine, and motherwort all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Moxonidine, nabilone, nalbuphine, and nitrous oxide all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely. 23. Norepinephrine decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 24. Nortriptyline, olanzapine, and olanzapine/samidorphan increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely. 25. Oliceridine, olopatadine (intranasal), opicapone, and orphenadrine all increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely. 26. Oxazepam, oxycodone, and oxymorphone increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Paliperidone, papaveretum, and papaverine increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Pegvisomant's effects are decreased by opium tincture through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Pentazocine and pentobarbital increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely. 30. Perphenazine, phenelzine, phenobarbital, phentermine, and phenylephrine (including oral) all interact with opium tincture, increasing sedation or toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely. 31. Pholcodine, pimozide, pirbuterol, and primidone increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Procarbazine increases the toxicity of opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Do not use within 14 days of MAOI use. 33. Prochlorperazine, promethazine, propofol, and propylhexedrine increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Protriptyline, quazepam, quetiapine, and ramelteon increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Rasagiline increases the toxicity of opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely for risks such as hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. 36. Rifampin decreases opium tincture levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 37. Risperidone, ropeginterferon alfa-2b, and sage increase sedation when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely. 38. Salmeterol decreases sedation, while opium tincture increases it. The interaction's effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 39. Skullcap and selegiline increase sedation or toxicity when combined with opium tincture. Avoid or use alternative drugs in serious cases. Monitor closely.
